note.text: A descriptive account helps the reader picture organised activities. Give the club's purpose, describe its setting and show what members do. Choose precise verbs and relevant details instead of an unconnected list. Use a consistent time frame and link the activities logically. Description can include small actions without becoming a full story about an unrelated journey. Avoid making claims about an actual school's club unless you have checked them.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: Our imaginary reading club meets in a bright classroom. Members arrange the books on a long table and read in small groups. A volunteer writes new words on the board, while another records book loans. The quiet discussion helps learners explain their favourite passages. At the end, everyone returns the materials to their places.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Plan setting, participants and activities. Ask whether each detail helps the reader see the club at work. Replace vague words such as nice with a precise observation. Keep the tense and subject references consistent.
